hi.strong_distractor: b — Option (b) 'Doctrine of Lapse' is the strongest distractor because the question is about Dalhousie-era British expansion, and students associate both terms with his tenure without distinguishing their mechanisms.
elimination_logic: रिक्त स्थान उस ढांचे का वर्णन करता है जो 'राज्य के क्षेत्रीय अस्तित्व को संरक्षित करते हुए उनके विदेशी और रक्षा मामलों पर ब्रिटिश सर्वोच्चता को स्थापित करता है' — यह सर्वोच्चता (paramountcy) की परिभाषा है।
(b) डाक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स (Doctrine of Lapse) को निरस्त करें: यह सिद्धांत राज्यों को संरक्षित नहीं करता था — यह उन्हें अवशोषित और समाप्त कर देता था। यह रिक्त स्थान में वर्णित अवधारणा का विपरीत है।

(a) सब्सिडियरी एलायंस (Subsidiary Alliance) को निरस्त करें: जबकि यह संधि राज्यों को संरक्षित करती थी, यह 1858 के बाद का वह ढांचा नहीं था जिसने डाक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स की जगह ली। यह संधि वेल्सली का उपकरण था, न कि 1857 के बाद की प्रतिस्थापन नीति।
(d) डाक्ट्रिन ऑफ फॉरफीचर (Doctrine of Forfeiture) को निरस्त करें: यह एक निर्मित शब्द है — ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक नीति में ऐसा कोई सिद्धांत नहीं था।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: मिश्रण का जाल इस प्रवृत्ति का फायदा उठाता है कि 'डाक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स' और 'डाक्ट्रिन ऑफ सर्वोच्चता' को ब्रिटिश साम्राज्यवाद के जुड़वां उपकरणों के रूप में देखा जाता है। जो छात्र दोनों नामों को एक साथ नोट्स में देखते हैं, वे याद नहीं रख पाते कि कौन सा सिद्धांत राज्यों को संरक्षित करता था और कौन सा समाप्त करता था। विकल्प (b) में डाक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स को रिक्त स्थान में भरना मुख्य जाल है — यह सही संबंध को उलट देता है।
hi.final_explanation:
डाक्ट्रिन ऑफ सर्वोच्चता (Doctrine of Paramountcy) डाक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स का उत्तराधिकारी ढांचा था — इसने विलय के अस्थिर प्रभाव के बिना नियंत्रण प्राप्त किया।

• विकल्प (a) — गलत: सब्सिडियरी एलायंस वेल्सली का 1800 से पहले का उपकरण था जो राज्यों को निर्भर बनाता था। जबकि यह राज्यों को संरक्षित करता था, यह 1858 के बाद डाक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स के प्रतिस्थापन का ढांचा नहीं था — यह संधि स्वयं राज्यों को विलय के लिए पात्र बनाती थी।
• विकल्प (b) — गलत: डाक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स अवधारणात्मक रूप से इसका विपरीत है — यह विलय के माध्यम से राज्यों को समाप्त करता था। इसे यहाँ डालना वाक्य का अर्थ उलट देता है।
• विकल्प (c) — सही: डाक्ट्रिन ऑफ सर्वोच्चता ने सभी भारतीय राज्यों पर ब्रिटिश सर्वोच्चता स्थापित की — उनके विदेशी नीति, रक्षा, और संचार को नियंत्रित करते हुए उन्हें आंतरिक शासन और क्षेत्रीय अस्तित्व बनाए रखने की अनुमति दी। यह 1858 के बाद का वह ढांचा था जिसने विलय की जगह प्रबंधित निर्भरता को लिया।
• विकल्प (d) — गलत: 'डाक्ट्रिन ऑफ फॉरफीचर' एक निर्मित शब्द है जिसका औपनिवेशिक इतिहास में कोई आधार नहीं है।

Value Addition:
• सर्वोच्चता के तहत, ब्रिटिशों ने आंतरिक मामलों में हस्तक्षेप का अधिकार दावा किया यदि 'दुशासन' साम्राज्य हितों को खतरे में डालता था — यह एक अवशिष्ट शक्ति थी जो राजाओं को आज्ञाकारी बनाए रखती थी।
• स्वतंत्रता के समय 550+ राजकीय राज्य सभी सर्वोच्चता युग के उत्पाद थे — वे इसलिए जीवित रहे क्योंकि विलय को छोड़ दिया गया था।
• सरदार पटेल ने 1947–48 में ब्रिटिश युग की सर्वोच्चता गारंटी वापस लेने की धमकी का उपयोग विलय सुनिश्चित करने के लिए किया।

shared.concept_anchor: Awadh annexation basis — misgovernance, not lapse

en.display_text:
The annexation of Awadh by Lord Dalhousie in 1856 was formally justified on the grounds of:

(a) The provisions of the Subsidiary Alliance of 1801, which had reserved British right of intervention
(b) The Doctrine of Lapse, because Nawab Wajid Ali Shah had died without a recognized natural heir
(c) A perceived military threat posed by Awadh's standing army to British territories in the Gangetic plain
(d) Misgovernance and administrative anarchy, which Dalhousie argued required British intervention in the interest of the population
en.strong_distractor: b — Option (b) attributes Awadh's annexation to the Doctrine of Lapse, which is the single most common misclassification. Students who have memorized 'Dalhousie's annexations' as a group apply the lapse label to all of them without distinguishing the specific legal basis.
elimination_logic: Recall that the Doctrine of Lapse required the ruler to die without a natural heir — this condition was not met in Awadh; Nawab Wajid Ali Shah had living successors.
Eliminate (b): the Doctrine of Lapse was inapplicable; Wajid Ali Shah had natural heirs. The lapse label is a conflation.
Eliminate (a): the Subsidiary Alliance was the instrument that made Awadh dependent, not the instrument that caused its annexation.
Eliminate (c): the 'military threat' justification was not the stated basis — Dalhousie explicitly used 'misgovernance and anarchy' as the formal rationale in his report.

Confirm (d): Awadh's annexation was explicitly justified on misgovernance grounds — Dalhousie's report argued the state was in administrative chaos and the population would benefit from British administration.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: This question exploits the most common and highest-stakes conflation in this topic. UPSC has tested the Awadh distinction multiple times because it is counterintuitive — the most politically significant and emotionally resonant Dalhousie annexation was NOT under the most famous doctrine. Students who memorize 'Dalhousie = Doctrine of Lapse' and apply it uniformly to all his annexations will select (b) and lose a mark with negative marking.
en.final_explanation:
Awadh's annexation is the definitional counter-example to the Doctrine of Lapse — it demonstrates that Dalhousie had multiple justifications available and used them selectively.

• Option (a) — Incorrect: The Subsidiary Alliance was the earlier instrument under which Awadh became a dependent state (from 1801). It was not the basis of the 1856 annexation.
• Option (b) — Incorrect: The Doctrine of Lapse required the ruler to lack a natural heir. Nawab Wajid Ali Shah had successors — the doctrine was legally inapplicable. This is the critical distinction that makes Awadh unique among Dalhousie's major annexations.
• Option (c) — Incorrect: While Awadh's military capacity was a concern, the formal and stated justification in Dalhousie's annexation report was misgovernance and the welfare of Awadh's population — not a military threat.
• Option (d) — Correct: Dalhousie's report on Awadh argued that the Nawab's administration was characterized by 'anarchy, oppression, and misgovernance,' and that the British were obligated to intervene on behalf of the population.

Value Addition:
• Awadh's annexation in February 1856 was the last major territorial acquisition before the 1857 revolt broke out in May 1857.
• Wajid Ali Shah was exiled to Calcutta — his wife, Begum Hazrat Mahal, stayed and led the Lucknow resistance in 1857.
• Awadh's large, unemployed military force (its ruler's private army) joined the revolt — making misgovernance the most politically consequential of Dalhousie's justifications.

• अवध का विलय फरवरी 1856 में हुआ था, जो मई 1857 में हुए विद्रोह से पहले अंतिम प्रमुख क्षेत्रीय अधिग्रहण था।

en.display_text:
Consider the following statements about the Doctrine of Lapse and the 1857 revolt:

1. Nana Sahib's denial of pension was directly linked to the British policy of rejecting adopted heirs for political succession — the same principle that underlay the Doctrine of Lapse.
2. The psychological insecurity created by the Doctrine of Lapse among surviving princely rulers — the fear that any succession irregularity could result in British annexation — contributed to a broad climate of political anxiety that facilitated the 1857 revolt.
3. The 1857 revolt was primarily a sepoy mutiny driven by the greased cartridge controversy, and historians have established that the Doctrine of Lapse had no meaningful causal role in the revolt.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 only
(b) 1 and 2 only
(c) 2 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: Nana Sahib's denial of pension was directly linked to the British policy of rejecting adopted heirs for political succession — the same principle that underlay the Doctrine of Lapse.
statement_analysis.reason: The rejection of Nana Sahib's pension claim explicitly invoked the argument that adopted sons did not inherit political entitlements — the identical logic used to reject adopted heirs under the Doctrine of Lapse.

statement_analysis.statement: The psychological insecurity created by the Doctrine of Lapse among surviving princely rulers — the fear that any succession irregularity could result in British annexation — contributed to a broad climate of political anxiety that facilitated the 1857 revolt.
statement_analysis.reason: Even rulers not directly threatened saw the doctrine as an existential danger; this generalized fear weakened loyalty to British authority and made rulers and their courts more sympathetic to anti-British mobilization.

statement_analysis.statement: The 1857 revolt was primarily a sepoy mutiny driven by the greased cartridge controversy, and historians have established that the Doctrine of Lapse had no meaningful causal role in the revolt.
statement_analysis.reason: Historians across multiple schools (nationalist, Marxist, and many mainstream) recognize the Doctrine of Lapse as a significant structural cause of the revolt. The 'no meaningful causal role' claim contradicts the historical consensus.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option (d) suggesting all three are correct is very tempting because the first two statements are accurate, and many students who know the greased cartridge was the trigger accept Statement 3's framing as a 'primary cause' argument without noticing the absolute denial of the doctrine's causal role.
elimination_logic: Verify Statement 1: pension denial using the adopted-heir rejection logic is explicitly documented in Nana Sahib's case. Correct.
Verify Statement 2: the generalized insecurity among all princely rulers is historically recognized as a structural climate facilitating revolt. Correct.

Examine Statement 3: the claim that the Doctrine of Lapse 'had no meaningful causal role' is directly contradicted by both nationalist and Marxist historiography, and by the documented grievances of key revolt leaders (Nana Sahib, Rani Lakshmibai). Incorrect.
Statements 1 and 2 correct; Statement 3 incorrect — option (b).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 3 exploits the 'greased cartridge as primary cause' framing that students absorb from introductory accounts of 1857. By presenting the cartridge controversy as the exclusive cause and denying the doctrine any role, it tests whether students can distinguish between 'immediate trigger' and 'structural cause.' Most historians treat the cartridge as the trigger within a deeper structural context — categorically denying the doctrine's role is historically incorrect.
en.final_explanation:
The Doctrine of Lapse's role in causing the 1857 revolt is multi-layered — individual grievances, class displacement, and systemic fear all operated simultaneously.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Nana Sahib's pension denial applied the same adopted-heir rejection logic as the Doctrine of Lapse — demonstrating how the policy extended beyond territorial annexation to individual dispossession. His subsequent revolt leadership directly traces to this grievance.
• Statement 2 — Correct: The doctrine created existential anxiety among all remaining princely rulers. Any succession complication — a dying ruler without a clear natural heir — became a potential trigger for annexation. This ambient fear made the broader princely class politically alienated.
• Statement 3 — Incorrect: Categorically denying the doctrine's causal role contradicts the historiographical mainstream. Nationalist historians like R.C. Majumdar identified it as a central cause; even balanced historians recognize it as a major structural grievance alongside the cartridge controversy, economic distress, and religious fears.

Value Addition:
• The 1857 revolt had three layers of causation: immediate trigger (cartridges), structural grievances (lapse, annexations, economic exploitation), and ideological context (fear of conversion, loss of cultural identity).
• Key revolt leaders connected to the Doctrine: Nana Sahib (pension denial), Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi annexation), Begum Hazrat Mahal (Awadh annexation).
• The British post-1857 recognition of the doctrine as provocative is itself evidence of its causal role — they abandoned it precisely because it had fueled revolt.

• कथन 3 — गलत: डोक्ट्रिन की कारणात्मक भूमिका को पूरी तरह नकारना इतिहासलेखन की मुख्यधारा के विपरीत है। राष्ट्रीयवादी इतिहासकार जैसे आर.सी. मजूमदार ने इसे एक केंद्रीय कारण माना; संतुलित इतिहासकार भी इसे कार्ट्रिज विवाद, आर्थिक संकट और धार्मिक भय के साथ एक प्रमुख संरचनात्मक शिकायत के रूप में मानते हैं।

Value Addition:
• 1857 के विद्रोह के तीन स्तर थे: तत्काल ट्रिगर (कार्ट्रिज), संरचनात्मक शिकायतें (लैप्स, अधिग्रहण, आर्थिक शोषण), और वैचारिक संदर्भ (धर्मांतरण का भय, सांस्कृतिक पहचान का नुकसान)।
• डोक्ट्रिन से जुड़े प्रमुख विद्रोह नेता: नाना साहिब (पेंशन अस्वीकृति), रानी लक्ष्मीबाई (झांसी अधिग्रहण), बेगम हजरत महल (अवध अधिग्रहण)।
• 1857 के बाद ब्रिटिशों द्वारा डोक्ट्रिन को उत्तेजक मानकर त्यागना स्वयं इसके कारणात्मक प्रभाव का प्रमाण है।

en.display_text:
Which of the following correctly describes the legal and statutory basis of the Doctrine of Lapse as applied by Lord Dalhousie?

(a) It was formally enacted under the Charter Act of 1853, which granted the Governor-General authority to deny adoption rights in dependent states
(b) It was codified under the Government of India Act of 1853 as a specific provision governing succession in subsidiary states
(c) It had no formal legislative or statutory backing and was implemented entirely as an executive administrative policy under the Governor-General's authority
(d) It was authorized by a Doctrine of Paramountcy Act passed by the British Parliament in the 1840s, granting the Company control over succession in dependent states
en.strong_distractor: a — Option (a) references the 'Charter Act of 1853,' which was a real piece of legislation and the last Company charter renewal before 1857. Students who associate 1853 with Dalhousie's active period and a real Act will find this option highly credible even though the Charter Act of 1853 did not codify the Doctrine of Lapse.
elimination_logic: Recall the fundamental nature of the Doctrine of Lapse: it was an administrative policy of the executive, not a legislative enactment. No Act of Parliament or Company statute formally created it.

Eliminate (a): the Charter Act of 1853 was real but concerned the Company's governance structure (it opened Indian civil services to competition, for example) — it did not codify the Doctrine of Lapse.

Eliminate (b): the Government of India Act of 1853 is a fabricated title — the relevant 1853 legislation was the Charter Act, not a 'Government of India Act'; in any case, neither codified the doctrine.
Eliminate (d): no such 'Doctrine of Paramountcy Act' was enacted in the 19th century — paramountcy operated as an extra-legal claim, not a statutory framework.
Confirm (c): the Doctrine of Lapse had no formal legislative backing; it was purely an executive administrative policy implemented through the Governor-General's authority.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The Charter Act of 1853 is a real and prominent piece of colonial legislation associated with Dalhousie's era (it opened civil services to competition and renewed the Company's charter). Students who study the act in a different context may instinctively accept option (a) as plausible, not realizing that the doctrine was never given statutory form. The plausible-fabrication trap works because the Act exists, the year matches, and Dalhousie's tenure coincides — only the content claim is false.
en.final_explanation:
The Doctrine of Lapse occupies an unusual space in colonial legal history: it was enormously consequential but entirely without formal statutory authorization.

• Option (a) — Incorrect: The Charter Act of 1853 was real legislation — it renewed the Company's charter for an indefinite period and opened Indian civil services to competitive examination. It did not address, codify, or authorize the Doctrine of Lapse in any provision.
• Option (b) — Incorrect: 'Government of India Act of 1853' is a fabricated title. The significant 1853 legislation was the Charter Act. Neither existed in the form described nor authorized the doctrine.
• Option (c) — Correct: The Doctrine of Lapse had no legislative backing whatsoever. It was implemented as an executive administrative policy by the Governor-General, using arguments about the nature of dependent sovereignty. This is precisely what made it legally vulnerable and politically contested.
• Option (d) — Incorrect: No 'Doctrine of Paramountcy Act' was enacted in the 19th century. Paramountcy was also an extra-legal claim, not a statute.

Value Addition:
• The absence of legislative backing made the doctrine dependent on the Governor-General's discretionary authority — and equally dependent on the Court of Directors' approval.
• After 1858, the Crown's relationship with princely states was also never fully codified — paramountcy remained an extra-legal doctrine too.
• The informality of both doctrines made the 1947 integration legally complex — there was no statute to repeal, only political agreements to negotiate.

(a) को निरस्त करें: चार्टर अधिनियम 1853 वास्तविक था लेकिन कंपनी के शासन ढांचे से संबंधित था (जैसे, इसने भारतीय सिविल सेवा में प्रतियोगिता खोली) — इसने डोक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स को विधिवत रूप से स्थापित नहीं किया।

(b) को निरस्त करें: 'गवर्नमेंट ऑफ इंडिया एक्ट 1853' एक काल्पनिक शीर्षक है — 1853 का संबंधित कानून चार्टर अधिनियम था, न कि 'गवर्नमेंट ऑफ इंडिया एक्ट'; वैसे भी, किसी ने भी इस डोक्ट्रिन को विधिवत रूप से स्थापित नहीं किया।
(d) को निरस्त करें: 19वीं सदी में ऐसा कोई 'डोक्ट्रिन ऑफ पैरामाउंटसी एक्ट' पारित नहीं हुआ — पैरामाउंटसी एक अतिरिक्त-वैधानिक दावा था, कोई सांविधिक ढांचा नहीं।
(c) को पुष्टि करें: डोक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स का कोई औपचारिक विधायी समर्थन नहीं था; यह पूरी तरह से गवर्नर-जनरल के अधिकार के तहत एक कार्यकारी प्रशासनिक नीति थी।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: चार्टर अधिनियम 1853 डलहौजी के युग से जुड़ा एक वास्तविक और प्रमुख औपनिवेशिक कानून है (इसने सिविल सेवा में प्रतियोगिता खोली और कंपनी के चार्टर का नवीनीकरण किया)। जो छात्र इसे अलग संदर्भ में पढ़ते हैं, वे सहज रूप से विकल्प (a) को संभावित मान सकते हैं, यह न समझते हुए कि डोक्ट्रिन को कभी विधिवत रूप नहीं दिया गया। यह संभावित-काल्पनिक जाल इसलिए काम करता है क्योंकि अधिनियम मौजूद है, वर्ष मेल खाता है, और डलहौजी का कार्यकाल भी मेल खाता है — केवल सामग्री दावा गलत है।
hi.final_explanation:
डोक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स औपनिवेशिक कानूनी इतिहास में एक असामान्य स्थिति रखता है: यह अत्यंत प्रभावशाली था लेकिन पूरी तरह से बिना औपचारिक सांविधिक प्राधिकरण के था।

• विकल्प (a) — गलत: चार्टर अधिनियम 1853 वास्तविक कानून था — इसने कंपनी के चार्टर को अनिश्चितकाल के लिए नवीनीकृत किया और भारतीय सिविल सेवा में प्रतियोगी परीक्षा खोली। इसने डोक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स को किसी प्रावधान में संबोधित, स्थापित या अधिकृत नहीं किया।
• विकल्प (b) — गलत: 'गवर्नमेंट ऑफ इंडिया एक्ट 1853' एक काल्पनिक शीर्षक है। महत्वपूर्ण 1853 का कानून चार्टर अधिनियम था। न तो ऐसा कोई कानून था और न ही इस डोक्ट्रिन को अधिकृत किया।
• विकल्प (c) — सही: डोक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स का कोई विधायी समर्थन नहीं था। इसे गवर्नर-जनरल द्वारा कार्यकारी प्रशासनिक नीति के रूप में लागू किया गया, जो आश्रित संप्रभुता की प्रकृति पर आधारित तर्कों का उपयोग करता था। यही इसे कानूनी रूप से कमजोर और राजनीतिक रूप से विवादित बनाता था।
• विकल्प (d) — गलत: 19वीं सदी में कोई 'डोक्ट्रिन ऑफ पैरामाउंटसी एक्ट' पारित नहीं हुआ। पैरामाउंटसी भी एक अतिरिक्त-वैधानिक दावा था, कोई कानून नहीं।

Value Addition:
• विधायी समर्थन की अनुपस्थिति ने डोक्ट्रिन को गवर्नर-जनरल के विवेकाधिकार पर निर्भर बना दिया — और समान रूप से कोर्ट ऑफ डायरेक्टर्स की मंजूरी पर भी।
• 1858 के बाद, राजसी राज्यों के साथ क्राउन का संबंध भी कभी पूरी तरह से विधिवत नहीं किया गया — पैरामाउंटसी भी एक अतिरिक्त-वैधानिक डोक्ट्रिन बनी रही।
• दोनों डोक्ट्रिन की अनौपचारिकता ने 1947 के एकीकरण को कानूनी रूप से जटिल बना दिया — कोई कानून रद्द करने के लिए नहीं था, केवल राजनीतिक समझौते करने थे।

shared.concept_anchor: British reversal of lapse — strategic not moral motivation

en.display_text:
Assertion (a): Following the Revolt of 1857, the British government through Queen Victoria's Proclamation formally recognized the right of Indian rulers to adopt heirs for succession, abandoning the position that had enabled the Doctrine of Lapse.

Reason (R): The Doctrine of Lapse had embodied a legal contradiction — the British recognized Hindu personal law (including adoption) in their civil courts but denied its application for political succession, a hypocrisy that was a source of widespread grievance among Indian rulers and their subjects.

Which of the following is correct?

(a) Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A
(b) Both A and R are correct, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
(c) A is correct but R is incorrect
(d) A is incorrect but R is correct
en.strong_distractor: a — Option (a) is the strongest distractor because students who know both A and R are correct will instinctively assume the moral argument (R) caused the policy reversal (a), without asking whether the British acted out of moral recognition or strategic self-interest.
elimination_logic: Step 1: Is Assertion (a) correct? — Yes. Queen Victoria's 1858 Proclamation did explicitly recognize adoption rights and formally reversed the Doctrine of Lapse's position on succession.

Step 2: Is Reason (R) correct? — Yes. The British did recognize a contradiction between applying Hindu personal law in civil courts and rejecting adoption for political succession — this was indeed identified as a grievance.

Step 3: Does R causally explain A? — No. The British abandoned the Doctrine of Lapse primarily for strategic reasons — the 1857 revolt had demonstrated that annexation created dangerous enemies. The recognition of legal contradiction was a grievance among Indians, not the motivating factor in the British policy reversal. The reversal was strategic, not an act of moral correction.
Both A and R are correct, but R does not explain A — option (b).
en.final_explanation:
This question tests whether students distinguish between what motivated British policy reversal (strategy) and what the grievances about the doctrine were (legal contradiction).

Assertion (a): Queen Victoria's Proclamation of 1858 explicitly recognized the right of Indian rulers to adopt heirs for succession purposes, formally abandoning the position that had underlain the Doctrine of Lapse. A is correct.

Reason (R): The Doctrine of Lapse involved a legal contradiction — the British recognized Hindu adoption in civil and family law while denying it for political succession. This inconsistency was a documented grievance and was noted by Indian political observers and colonial critics. R is correct.

Causal relationship: R does not explain A. The British abandoned the doctrine primarily because the 1857 revolt had dramatically demonstrated the political cost of annexation — loyal princely states were now seen as a strategic necessity, not an obstacle. The policy reversal was driven by self-interest and strategic recalculation, not by a moral recognition of the legal contradiction. While the contradiction was real, acknowledging it was not the reason for the 1858 proclamation.

Value Addition:
• The irony noted by historians: the Doctrine of Lapse was abandoned 'because it worked too well' — it successfully annexed states but created a resistance that nearly ended British rule.
• The strategic logic of post-1858 princely state policy was that loyal princes served as a buffer and legitimizing class for British authority.
• The legal contradiction (recognizing Hindu adoption in civil law but not political succession) was never formally resolved — it was simply bypassed by the 1858 policy guarantee.

कथन (a): क्वीन विक्टोरिया का 1858 का उद्घोष स्पष्ट रूप से भारतीय शासकों को उत्तराधिकार के लिए वारिस गोद लेने का अधिकार मानता है, और Doctrine of Lapse की उस स्थिति को औपचारिक रूप से त्याग देता है जो इसके आधार थी। A सही है।

कारण (R): Doctrine of Lapse में एक कानूनी विरोधाभास था — ब्रिटिश नागरिक और पारिवारिक कानून में हिंदू गोद लेने को मान्यता देते थे जबकि राजनीतिक उत्तराधिकार के लिए इसे अस्वीकार करते थे। यह असंगति एक दर्ज शिकायत थी और इसे भारतीय राजनीतिक पर्यवेक्षकों और औपनिवेशिक आलोचकों ने नोट किया था। R सही है।

कारणात्मक संबंध: R, A की व्याख्या नहीं करता। ब्रिटिशों ने यह सिद्धांत मुख्य रूप से इसलिए त्याग दिया क्योंकि 1857 के विद्रोह ने अधिग्रहण की राजनीतिक लागत को नाटकीय रूप से दिखाया — वफादार रियासतों को अब रणनीतिक आवश्यकता के रूप में देखा गया, बाधा के रूप में नहीं। नीति परिवर्तन स्वार्थ और रणनीतिक पुनर्मूल्यांकन से प्रेरित था, कानूनी विरोधाभास की नैतिक मान्यता से नहीं। जबकि विरोधाभास वास्तविक था, उसे स्वीकार करना 1858 के उद्घोष का कारण नहीं था।
